Subject: Pilot requirements and data isolation needs (MedAlign)

Hi Diego / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the execs want to move a small pilot forward but with strict isolation and data residency controls. High level asks:
- Pilot target: ~50 steady RPS (inference calls), burst to 120 RPS; p95 latency target ~350ms for short-generation use cases.
- Data type: PHI-containing records; customer requires isolated tenancy or air-gapped private control plane.
- Retention & audit: 90-day token-level logs retained, SOC2 + additional questionnaire answers needed.
- Timeline: pilot kickoff mid-November; procurement team needs a workback plan and high-level cost delta between dedicated and private deployments.

Attached: medalign_poc_requirements.pdf (short list). Can you provide sizing scenarios and a fallback / escalation ladder (e.g., dedicated reserve + burst lanes, hosted fallbacks)? Also please include expected delivery lead-time for Private (VPC/on-prem) vs Dedicated.

Appreciate a concise recommendation we can show the CISO.

Diego / Alice — attached is a first-pass sizing table (see estimated_gpu_footprint.xlsx). Key assumptions up front:
- Model assumption: 7B-ish instruction-tuned encoder-decoder for short-generation (avg 120 tokens).
- Typical token-throughput: ~250 tokens/sec per A10G-equivalent for short context; H100 improves throughput ~2–3x depending on kernel set and quantization.
- For the pilot (50 steady RPS, bursts to 120): baseline compute needs ~6 A10G-equivalent GPUs with autoscaling headroom to 10; if we use H100-equivalents, that drops to ~3–4 nodes.
- For production-scale (500 steady RPS): baseline ~60 A10G-equivalents (~20 H100-equivalents).

Private vs Dedicated:
- Dedicated (reserved pool): Fastest to provision (2–3 weeks), lower ops overhead, Redwood manages control plane, customer data segmented at tenant level. Good if customer accepts vendor-managed networking.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Stronger isolation (air-gap possible), customer-managed networking/KMS, longer delivery (4–12 weeks), higher engineering handoff and testing. Operational cost uplift estimated +25–40% vs Dedicated.

Fallback / tiering ladder (recommended):
1) Tier A — Dedicated reserved H100 pool (primary): low-latency, SLA-backed.
2) Tier B — Dedicated burst preemptible nodes (cheaper spot instances) for transient load spikes — ~20–30% cheaper with lower SLA.
3) Tier C — Hosted small-model fallback (quantized 4-bit variant) served from standard hosted API to keep availability while reducing quality for extreme overflow.

I'll add a simple cost delta sheet for Dedicated vs Private (conservative ops uplift + longer lead times).

Marissa

Adding engineering tradeoffs and a quick sizing rationale:

Sizing rationale (back-of-envelope):
- Pilot (50 RPS, avg 120 tokens, 1.2s per request CPU-bound portion): ~6 A10G-equivalents => supports ~60 steady RPS with modest headroom. If we enable continuous batching + KV prefix caching we can reduce effective GPU work by ~15–25% (depends on request overlap).
- Production (500 RPS): linear scaling suggests ~60 A10G-equivalents; with OPTIMIZED kernels + quantization we can target ~40–45 A10G-equivalents.

Node types & delivery:
- H100-equivalent: best p95 and lowest node count; provisioning time 2–3 weeks for Dedicated, 6–10 weeks for Private (if air-gapped).
- A10G-equivalent: longer tail on p95; lower per-node cost; useful as burst tier.

Fallback policies (technical):
- Policy 1: Auto-failover from Dedicated to burst preemptible nodes in same region (automated routing, 1–2 minute failover).
- Policy 2: If reserved + burst exhausted, route to hosted fallback model (smaller quantized variant) — preserve availability but degraded quality.
- Policy 3: For Private deployments, if on-prem capacity short, enable cross-region dedicated fallback (requires UAT sign-off for data flow).

Security notes:
- For PHI customers insist on customer-managed KMS and token scrubbing at the edge before routing into shared planes. Private on-prem is the cleanest path for compliance but costs ops/time.

I left comments in the workbook on assumptions.

Karthik
Director, Deal Engineering — Redwood Inference

Summarizing and next steps for MedAlign (to be shared with the CISO/procurement):

1) Sizing (pilot): Recommend Dedicated reserved H100-equivalent pool sized for the pilot: 4 H100-equivalents (expected to meet 50 RPS steady, burst to 120, p95 ~300–350ms) with autoscale to 8 for short bursts. Estimated footprint in workbook (sheet: medalign_v1).

2) Private vs Dedicated delta (short bullets):
- Cost: Private ops uplift +30% (range 25–40%); Dedicated baseline lower TCO for managed networking.
- Delivery: Dedicated 2–3 weeks; Private (VPC) 3–4 weeks; Private on-prem / air-gapped 8–12 weeks.
- Ops & compliance: Private gives the cleanest isolation and customer-managed KMS; Dedicated gives tenant-level isolation with Redwood-managed networking and faster time-to-value.

3) Fallback ladder: Tier A — Dedicated reserved H100 pool; Tier B — Dedicated burst/spot nodes; Tier C — Hosted quantized fallback model.

4) Commercial & gating: We will produce a short MAP and cost-delta table for Procurement (Aditya) and surface SOC2 evidence + token-logging retention options. Karthik: flag any gating items for a Nov 15 pilot.

I'll publish the updated workbook and a one-pager for the CISO by EOD tomorrow. Please review the attached files and call out any factual changes.
